name: Pu Luong
provinceNote: From 1 July 2025, Resolution 1686 created xã Pù Luông from old Thành Sơn, Lũng Niêm, and Thành Lâm. That commune is only part of the valley. Bản Hiêu and Son, Bá, and Mười sit in xã Cổ Lũng.
dotReason: Worth a special trip for the limestone rice valley
summary: Sleep in a stilt house when the morning is terraced rice on a limestone valley in Thanh Hoa. Stay if that valley is the trip. Go to Mai Chau if you wanted Bản Lác, and to Ninh Binh if you wanted the boats. Hanoi is about 160 km on Vietnam Tourism and about 210 km on the conservation pages. Those pages print 17,662 hectares. The 2021 decision prints 16,986.16 hectares. A gate fee is check on arrival.
getThere: Hanoi by road, about 160 km or about 210 km. Rail is check on arrival.
seoTitle: Pu Luong travel guide — a night in the rice valley
seoDescription: Rice terraces and a stilt house in Thanh Hoa, about 160 km or about 210 km from Hanoi, green in late May to early June and gold in September and October.
intro: You wake in a stilt house to terrace walls, a limestone ridge, and mist on the fields. This is Pù Luông Nature Reserve, the valley in Thanh Hoa. The morning is the crop on the slopes and the posts under the house.

Stay if that valley at breakfast is the trip. Go to Mai Chau if Bản Lác is the trip. That hamlet stays on the Mai Chau page. Go to Ninh Binh if the boats are the trip. From 1 July 2025, Resolution 1686 made xã Pù Luông out of old Thành Sơn, Lũng Niêm, and Thành Lâm. That commune is only part of the valley. Bản Hiêu and the hamlets Son, Bá, and Mười sit in xã Cổ Lũng.

The conservation pages put the reserve about 210 km from Hanoi and print 17,662 hectares, of which 13,320 hectares are strict protection and 4,343 hectares are restoration. Those two zones add to 17,663. Vietnam Tourism prints about 160 km southwest, and a limousine of about 4.5 hours from Giáp Bát or Mỹ Đình. The 2021 decision prints 16,986.16 hectares. Both distances stand, and both area figures stand. No minute count was printed beside either kilometer. A car or a motorbike hired in Hanoi is the usual road. No train into the valley was found, so the rail time is check on arrival. The mistake is booking the neighbor when the photograph you wanted is this valley in the morning.
gettingAround: Bicycles are what Vietnam Tourism says visitors are offered, on the valley road, with steeper lanes if you want them. Homestays often lend them without a charge. That “often” is one page, and a hire sheet was not opened, so the charge is check on arrival. A local motorbike is occasional, not the usual hire. No commune bus was named. Many hamlets want cash, on one commercial guide.

The 2021 scheme puts the management board in thị trấn Cành Nàng, now inside xã Bá Thước, and it plans a visitor center there and at khu phố Vận Tải. This pass did not open a page that says the center is open. Thác Hiêu is about 25 km from Cành Nàng on the provincial culture page. That kilometer has no second source. The waterfall is in old Cổ Lũng, now xã Cổ Lũng. One page describes five small falls and blue-green water. Another describes a stream of about 800 metres that splits into two branches and meets again above a pool. Both descriptions stand. A walk of 6–8 km and 2–4 hours from Bản Đôn is one commercial guide. Check on arrival.

The summit walk is a separate two-day trek inside special-use forest, from bản Pù Luông to bản Báng, about 11 km, with nearly 2 km steeper than 35 degrees, in a limited group. VietNamNet prints the height as 1,700 m and, in another sentence, as higher than 1,700 m. Vietnam Tourism prints 1,700 m. The conservation page says the Thai name means the highest peak. The airline guide says it means “núi lớn”. Both glosses stand. Minutes from Bản Đôn were not printed. A guide fee is check on arrival. Newcomers are told to walk with a group or a local guide. Walk the summit only in that limited group. The species lists are the reserve inventory. They do not schedule an animal on the path.

A provincial article dated 19 Oct 2026 describes the Vietnam Jungle Marathon through forest, hamlets, terraces, and bamboo bridges, with the start and finish at Làng Leo. Printed distances are 70 km, 50 km, 25 km, and 10 km. The 70 km start on that page is 04:00. The race morning’s calendar date is check on arrival. The article date is not the gun time.

stayAreas.name: Ban Don
stayAreas.summary: Stilt-house homestays in old Thành Lâm, now inside xã Pù Luông. Terraces at the foot of the hill, and a campfire, rượu cần, xòe, and khắp in the evening. Room rates are check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Ban Hieu
stayAreas.summary: Stilt houses around Bản Hiêu, old Cổ Lũng, now xã Cổ Lũng, for the walk toward Thác Hiêu. Room rates are check on arrival.

eat: The meal is in the stilt house: Cổ Lũng duck, forest bamboo, hill chicken, and rượu cần. Phố Đoàn is a roadside market on Thursday and Sunday. No licensed photograph of a plate was found, so none of these is a dish card. Stall prices are check on arrival.

Cổ Lũng duck is described as low in fat, eaten boiled, grilled, or in a sour soup. One provincial writer dips the boiled bird in chẩm chéo, built from rang mắc khén, fresh chili, ginger, salt, and herbs. The Bản Đôn list says vịt cỏ and does not say it is the same bird. Forest bamboo is măng rừng at the house, măng khô at the market, and măng đắng on the airline guide, eaten there with a dip or fried with forest pork. The three names are not one recipe. Hill chicken is described as firm, with crisp skin, grilled with lá mắc mật. The summit-camp supper names grilled chicken, xôi đồ, rượu ngô, and rượu chuối. That camp rice is not the same line as xôi tím, which Bản Đôn lists without saying where the color comes from.

Stream fish, grilled with forest leaves, and cơm lam, glutinous rice in a bamboo tube, are on the airline guide only. Rock snail is ốc đá at Bản Đôn. The market article also says ốc suối and ốc núi. The airline guide calls it a rainy-season snail, steamed with lemongrass or fried with lime leaf. Bản Đôn does not print a season. Both stand. Forest pig is lợn rừng on the provincial list and lợn cỏ on the airline guide. They are not merged into one breed. Pumpkin greens and chayote tips are on the Bản Đôn meal, with no method printed. A breakfast hour was not printed. Check on arrival. Thịt treo gác bếp is named among highland-market goods, not only this valley, so it is check on arrival as a Pu Luong recipe.
interestsBody: The terraces are the reason to sleep here. Late May to early June is the green crop on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are the gold crop on those pages. A provincial trekking note calls both windows golden.
The houses are on stilts, in Thai and Muong hamlets. Bản Đôn is the usual base. The evening is a campfire on the hamlet floor, not a bar street.
Thác Hiêu, the summit walk, Phố Đoàn, and the bicycle day are real, and they are not cards. No licensed photograph of those subjects was found.

interestGroups.title: Terraces on two calendars
interestGroups.summary: For the rice on the slopes, green in one window and gold in the other.
body: Late May to early June is the green young rice on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are the ripe gold crop on those same pages. A provincial trekking note calls both May–June and September–October ripe and golden. Bản Đôn is busiest in February, March, September, and October. Morning is the hour for mist on the hills. A fixed gate hour for the fields was not printed. Check on arrival.
Bamboo water wheels lift stream water onto the fields. Vietnam Tourism calls them a Thai marker. They are scattered. No single wheel has an address on that page.

cards.title: Valley terraces
cards.summary: Come for the crop on the limestone slopes. Late May to early June is green. September and October are gold. One trekking note calls both windows golden.

interestGroups.title: Stilt houses of the Thai and Muong
interestGroups.summary: For a night in a house on posts, with the fire on the hamlet floor.
body: Vietnam Tourism says the reserve is home to Thai and Muong people and that the houses are on stilts. Bản Đôn, in old Thành Lâm and now inside xã Pù Luông, is mostly Thai. The evening there is a campfire, rượu cần, xòe Thái, and khắp. Xòe is also held for guests on ordinary nights, not only on a festival date. A start time was not printed. Check on arrival. A feature prints a UNESCO date of 15 Dec 2021 for xòe Thái. The UNESCO page was not opened. The night here is the hamlet circle.

Old Thành Lâm is where a political-school page names lễ hội Căm Mương, lễ hội cơm mới, and a culture day, without dates. A 2022 culture day is what the xòe feature describes. Those dates are check on arrival. Resort names on the provincial Bản Đôn page are not picks.

cards.title: A house on posts
cards.summary: Sleep in a Thai or Muong stilt house. Bản Đôn is the usual base, with the fire after dark.

interestGroups.title: A short walk with a guide
interestGroups.summary: For hamlets and paths, with a guide if the valley is new to you.
body: A provincial trekking note separates a harder Son–Bá–Mười line and a Làng Bầm forest path from an easier walk, Bản Đôn to bản Ngòn and bản Leo, for people who want the hamlets more than the summit. It tells newcomers to take a guide. No guide fee was printed. Check on arrival. Son, Bá, and Mười are three hamlets in old Lũng Cao, now xã Cổ Lũng, not one viewpoint.

Thác Hiêu, the two-day summit, and the Thursday and Sunday market at Phố Đoàn are the other outings. No licensed photograph of the fall, the summit, or the market was found, so they are not cards. Pa Co pine, northern red pine, and Khuyn waterfall are named in the 2021 scheme. A visit with an hour was not found, so they are not pages.

cards.title: Hamlet paths
cards.summary: Walk the easier line between hamlets, with a guide if you are new here. The fee is check on arrival.

faqs.q: How far is Pu Luong from Hanoi?
faqs.a: The conservation pages print about 210 km. Vietnam Tourism prints about 160 km southwest, and a limousine of about 4.5 hours from Giáp Bát or Mỹ Đình. No minute count sits beside either kilometer. No rail timetable for the valley was opened. The train is check on arrival.

The figures disagree, so they are all printed. Decision 495 of 27 Mar 1999: 17,660 hectares. The conservation pages: 17,662 hectares, with 13,320 strict and 4,343 restoration. Decision 3001 of 8 Nov 2001: 16,982.6 hectares. Decision 2463 of 16 Jul 2013: 17,171.03 hectares. Decision 1976 of 30 Oct 2014: 17,171.53 hectares. Decision 3392 of 31 Aug 2021: 16,986.16 hectares, with an appendix strict-protection subtotal of 10,953.27 hectares. The management page also prints strict 12,561.60, restoration 4,300.4, service 216.03, and other land 93.0, which add to the 2013 total rather than to 16,986.16. Vietnam Tourism says more than 17,600 hectares.

faqs.q: When is the rice, and when are the festivals?
faqs.a: Late May to early June is the green crop, and September and October are the gold crop, on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. A trekking note calls both windows golden. Lễ hội Căm Mương, the new-rice rite, and the valley culture day have no 2026 date on the pages opened. The Vietnam Jungle Marathon’s calendar date is check on arrival.

season.label: Two rice windows
season.note: Late May to early June is green young rice on the conservation pages and on Vietnam Tourism. September and October are ripe gold on those pages. A provincial trekking note calls both windows ripe and golden, cool, and with little rain. Bản Đôn is busiest in February, March, September, and October. Vietnam Tourism also says the valley is visitable in any month, and that summer stays cooler than the lowland because of limestone, forest, and few people. The airline guide says avoid July and August as storm months, with slippery roads. The conservation pages and Vietnam Tourism do not say that. A road-closure calendar was not opened. Check on arrival.
